correctness.rationale: For the sixteen-vertex binary hypercube Q4, independent construction verifies 280 connected/1540 disconnected four-sets, 64,558 nonempty cut faces, and acyclic 32,160-pair Morse matching across all 511,696 Hasse incidences with one critical vertex, 31 degree-ten and 206 degree-eleven cells. The Alexander dual has full two-skeleton, precisely 280 connected-fourset tetrahedra, and no higher simplices by absence of K2,3 in the cube. Exact integral sparse column elimination has 255 unit pivots in the 560x280 tetrahedron boundary, proving primitive image and free dual ranks H3=25, H2=200. Alexander duality yields free original H10=25,H11=200. In the Morse two-consecutive-degree CW complex these ranks force six unit Smith factors; pi10 of a wedge of S10 is Z31, so six unit-attached 10/11-cell pairs cancel, leaving the claimed wedge.

evidence: A general integer homology classification cannot imply a wedge decomposition in arbitrary CW complexes: nontrivial attaching maps may have zero Hurewicz image. Here the extra explicit high-degree Morse CW structure restricts attaching maps to pi10(vee S10)=Z31 and makes the homotopy upgrade valid. Total cut of cube uses independent foursets, not ordinary disconnected foursets.
Complete integral four-cut homology of binary hypercubes — COVERS integrally free Betti numbers and nonshellability, NOT the claimed wedge homotopy equivalence.
Topology of Cut Complexes of Graphs — Foundational definitions and other graph family results; no inspected homotopy theorem for this Q4 threshold.
